note: REGIME DOWNGRADED to NEUTRAL. The three-leg gate set on 2026-08-03 resolved 3-of-3 in favour of the downgrade on the Monday 3 Aug session. Leg 1 (Korea/Taiwan hold >50% of the 31 Jul record gain): PASSED - KOSPI closed 6,257.45, -338.00 (-5.12%), giving back ~338 of Friday's ~1,001-point gain, i.e. ~34%, retaining ~66%; TAIEX closed 43,386.41, +266.66 (+0.62%), retaining 100%+. Leg 2 (Brent stays below $90): PASSED emphatically - ~$83.7-83.9, a second consecutive ~5% down-leg. Leg 3 (30Y does not close above 5.35%): PASSED - 5.23%, -5bp. The escalation triggers (Iranian repudiation with Brent reclaiming $95; 30Y breaking 5.5%) did NOT fire. Per section 11's two-asset-class corroboration rule, the downgrade clears the bar by a wide margin: equities (Dow record 53,178.41 +1.3%, S&P 7,600.50 +1.5% within 0.1% of its record, Russell 2,981.91 +1.7% - breadth PARTICIPATING for the first time in weeks, the reverse of Friday's index-up/breadth-down tape), rates (10Y -6bp, 30Y -5bp), commodities (Brent -4.7%) and FX (yen +1.4%) all moved as a de-escalation story predicts. TWO THINGS THE DOWNGRADE DOES NOT SAY. (1) It is not an upgrade to risk-on: North Asia broke the OTHER way in the same session (KOSPI -5.12%, Nikkei -2.2%, TOPIX -2.8%) and the AI axis FRACTURED rather than resolving - Korea -5.12% / Taiwan +0.62% / Nasdaq +2.1% on one day, with memory weak (Samsung DX first-ever divisional loss, SK Hynix) and design/packaging strong (MediaTek and ASE limit-up, TSMC DOWN). (2) It was declared WITHOUT a credit confirmation - no HY OAS, no HYG/LQD, no ETF flows for a THIRD consecutive session, and no VIX close or 2Y close either. That is the single largest hole in this call and is stated as such in the brief. NEXT GATE (resolves on the 7 Aug payroll): escalate back toward stress if the 30Y closes above 5.5%, or if payrolls print above 150k with hot average hourly earnings alongside a hot 6 Aug unit-labour-costs print, or if Iran repudiates the Oman track and Brent reclaims $95; move toward risk-on only on a credit print confirming firmness PLUS a second session of positive US breadth.
growth: US firming, China softening - the divergence widened rather than closed. US ISM manufacturing 55.6 in July vs 54.0 consensus and 53.3 prior, the strongest factory print of the cycle: production 52.2->58.5, employment 49.7->52.8 (back to expansion), new export orders 48.5->53.0 (back to expansion), backlog 50.5->55.0, customers' inventories 'too low' at 40.7%. Against that, China's private RatingDog manufacturing PMI fell to 50.9 (prior 51.7, cons 51.9), a four-month low with output and new orders at four-month lows - converging DOWN toward the official NBS 49.2, gap narrowed ~2.5 -> ~1.7pts; its counterweights were new export orders back in expansion (first in three months) and the fastest employment growth since Aug 2023. Iron ore at ~US$94/t, a >1-year low from ~$110 three months ago (Fortescue -3.3% to an 11-month low), corroborates the Chinese-demand read. India was the region's cleanest winner: Nifty +1.60% / Sensex +0.70%, a fourth straight advance, with July FII inflows of Rs20,200 crore ending four months of selling.
inflation: Headline falling, core sticky - and the decoupling is now visible inside a single release. ISM prices paid eased 73.0 -> 71.1: a deceleration from a very high base, NOT deflation, with a majority of purchasing managers still paying more. Negative-comment drivers were pricing volatility 57%, the Iran conflict 43%, tariffs only 18%. Critically the July ISM already contains the war - the AUGUST print is where the crude collapse should first appear. Europe runs the other way for now: July HICP cited at 2.9% from 2.8% (secondary source), because energy enters the European print with a lag. Unverified link, second consecutive run: no diesel-crack print sourced, so with Russian refineries (Ufa, Saratov, Nizhnekamsk, Ryazan) at 2005-low runs the 'cheaper crude means cheaper fuel' chain remains unconfirmed.
liquidity: NOT SOURCED this run. Last H.4.1 read remains the week of 22 Jul (reserves 3,062bn, -80.6 w/w). No BTC ETF flow data sourced. This component is unchanged only in the sense that nothing new was retrieved - it is a gap, not a reading.
monetary_policy: Synchronised hawkish hold intact; FX is the active instrument and it was USED. Japan and the US CONFIRMED the joint yen intervention on the record - the first such operation since 2011 - and the yen rose 1.4% to 155.20, a near-three-month high, +3.8% across two sessions. Japan's equity market bore the entire cost: all 33 TSE sector groups lower, 212 of 225 Nikkei constituents down, transport equipment -5%, Toyota -5.3%, Suzuki -8%. That is a visible, observable transfer from currency stability to exporter earnings, and it is why Japan DIVERGED (fell 2.2%) on a day cheaper energy should have helped the G7's largest net energy importer. No central bank meets before the RBI on 5 Aug (hold at 5.25% expected). September Fed hike odds remain UNQUOTABLE - no reliable single reading was retrieved this run either. The week's policy risk is still data, not decisions: JOLTS 4 Aug, ISM Services 5 Aug, unit labour costs 6 Aug, payrolls 7 Aug.
fiscal_impulse: Insufficient data at the global level. Malaysia-specific and now empirically visible: the KLCI closed FLAT (+0.05% at 1,725.73) on a day crude fell ~5%, while the ringgit weakened to 4.0935/0975. The two oil channels separated cleanly for the first time - the fiscal/subsidy-relief channel (BIMB had 2026 fuel subsidies at RM40bn vs RM21.6bn budgeted, built on a 1H26 Brent average of $92.50 against a $65 Budget assumption) held the equity index, while the export-receipts channel hit the currency. No Negeri Sembilan election commentary appeared in any sourced market report - the political discount the desk was watching for did not visibly price.
risk_appetite: Improving in the West, breaking down in North Asia - and the Western improvement is the better-corroborated of the two. US: Dow record close 53,178.41 (+693.38, +1.3%), S&P 7,600.50 (+110.78, +1.5%) 0.1% below its 7,609.78 record, Nasdaq Composite 25,913.90 (+540.04, +2.1%), Russell 2000 2,981.91 (+50.57, +1.7%) - small caps LED, the reverse of Friday, which is the participation the desk said was missing. Megacaps still did heavy lifting (AMZN +4% to a $3trn market cap, META +6%, GOOGL and MSFT +5%, NVDA +3%) but were not the whole tape. Europe intraday showed a textbook input-cost-relief rotation (aero/defence +2.6%, autos +2.2%, luxury +1.7%, travel +1.6% vs energy -1%); no European close was sourced. North Asia: KOSPI -5.12% (large-cap memory unwind - the small-cap KOSDAQ ROSE +2.4%), Nikkei -2.2%, TOPIX -2.8%. Taiwan rose +0.62% but on a domestic rotation DOWN the cap scale (TPEx +4.32%) absorbing NT$19.19bn of foreign selling, with TSMC itself DOWN. NOT CONFIRMED: no VIX close was sourced (15.94 intraday at 09:15 ET).
credit: UNKNOWN - no print sourced for a THIRD consecutive session. Last reliable read remains HY OAS 287bp (29 Jul obs); HYG +0.29% vs LQD +0.18% on 30 Jul. Do not infer firmness from silence. This is the largest acknowledged hole in today's downgrade.
